reason: Both end at the right place (stop using, isolate, electrician/engineer, no live tests), but Conversation 2 actually engaged the homeowner, surfaced the key safety facts (faint electrical smell, boil-overs, kettle on same circuit) and gave a correct, practical isolation instruction at the wall cooker switch. Conversation 1 jumped straight to a boilerplate stop with no questions, an odd 'No—' opener and an 'unplug it' instruction that doesn't fit a built-in hob. Conversation 2 is marked down for overconfidence ('almost certainly earth-leakage', 'replace the damaged module') when the hidden truth is genuinely uncertain between leakage and overload, and neither asked which device trips, so the margin is only slight.
